answers.falsifier: with a pythonw.exe beside the executable, background_python('nt', executable=...) returns the pythonw.exe path, where it returned the python.exe path ; with no pythonw.exe beside it, and on posix, background_python returns the executable unchanged
answers.how: In cairn/tools/windowless_spawn/windowless_spawn.py background_python, where os_name is nt and a pythonw.exe sits beside the executable, return that path; else return the executable as now (posix unchanged). Update its docstring: the old guess about base interpreters stays recorded as refuted, and the pythonw launcher exits at once so a caller must not track the child by Popen.pid or poll. Red-first proof cairn/tools/windowless_spawn/proofs/test_background_python_is_pythonw_on_nt.py builds a scratch dir with python.exe and pythonw.exe and asserts the nt result is the pythonw path, the no-pythonw case returns the executable, and posix is unchanged; tooth 2 of 0156856b1fae (the live conhost tree measurement) turns green and is cited by the PROVEME note.
answers.title: a background child on Windows starts through pythonw so no console host sits in its tree
answers.traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: the console-in-tree claim was measured red and the fix is proven by the same measurement; Law 9: red is the default and tooth 2 stays the instrument.
answers.what: background_python on nt returns the pythonw.exe beside the interpreter when it exists, so a spawned background child owns no console host, and the proof says what a caller sees of it.
